newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends down sharply on weather, charts.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends down sharply on weather, charts.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended lower across the board Monday in a moderate session, undermined by a wave of technical sales and the prospect that mild weather this week would continue to pressure the cash.
December tumbled 8.9 cents to close at $2.573 per million British thermal units. January settled 8.7 cents lower at $2.557. Other deferreds ended down by 0.9 to 7.5 cents.

"The market has been keying off the weather, which could mean more downside near-term," said one Houston-based trader, adding it could be tough to rally with several days of relatively mild weather forecast for major consuming regions.

But while December broke a short-term up trendline today, opening the possibility of more selling near-term, some said they expected the spot contract to take a breather near next support in the $2.52 area, particularly after the 10 percent slide seen since Thursday when the $2.88 high was set.
Resistance was seen at Friday's high of $2.72, then at the $2.88 contract high and then at $2.92 and $2.98, prominent spot continuation chart highs set in late June and early July.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices were down about five cents Monday to about the $2.70 area. Midwest prices slipped almost a dime to the mid-$2.50s. New York city gate swing gas was quoted in the $3.05-3.10 area, off more than 15 cents.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip slumped another 5.3 cents to $2.133. NYMEX said 34,142 Hub contracts traded, down from Friday's revised tally of 28,093.
NYMEX December Alberta natgas closed one-half cent lower at $1.225, while deferreds were untraded. NYMEX said 37 Alberta contracts traded compared with 12 on Friday.
NYMEX Permian natgas again was untraded but December ended down by 10 cents at $2.44.

On the KCBT, December finished 8.7 cents lower at $2.473, while deferreds settled down by four to 10 cents. The December East/West spread narrowed by 0.2 cent to 10.0 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 46 contracts traded, down from Friday's total of 379.
